request.spec:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on

retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other

any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged

to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now merge one person into another from the person's row. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the merge test and the three other scenarios in the spec.

**How it works**
- Each person row has a new **Merge** cell with a `person-merge-into` select listing everyone on the sheet by name, and a `person-merge` button.
- The new endpoint is `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge`, with a body of `{ into: <id> }`. Its pipeline file is `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge.POST.yml`.
- It writes `PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>`, followed by the usual `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines when any figures change.

**Refusals.** A merge is refused, with the error shown on the row and nothing written, when:
- the user isn't a steward;
- the person is merged into themselves (they appear in their own select, as the request describes);
- either person is retired;
- no person to merge into is chosen.

**What happens to the merged person's data**
- **Claims** move to the other person, keeping their numbers and dates. They are moved oldest first, so they appear after the other person's claims in the order they were added. Each loses any statement-bound figure; settled claims keep their settled amount.
- **Name and aliases:** the merged name becomes a new alias of the other person, followed by the merged person's own aliases in their original order.
- **Patrons:**
  - The merged person's patrons are added to the other person's, leaving out the other person themselves and any repeats.
  - Anyone who named the merged person as patron now names the other person instead, again without repeats. A person never ends up as their own patron.
- **Pools:** the merged person's memberships move to the other person. Where the other person is already in the pool, the two shares are added together.
- **Dropped:** the merged person's statements, grades, holds, watchers and contact are deleted along with their row, which removes them from the list.

**Not handled:** stored per-period totals (`period_person_total`) and saved past-day snapshots (`sheet_day`) still refer to the merged person. The request didn't mention them and no test checks them.

The server changes are in `person/`: `MergeRequest`, `ValidateMergeRequest`, `CheckMerge`, `Merge`, `MergePerson`, `AuditPersonMerged`, `RespondWithMerge`, plus a new `merge` method in `PersonRepository`. The front end is `features/merge/PersonMerge.tsx` and `merge.slot.tsx`.
